arxiv-2107-00171.title: p-wave superconductivity and the axi-planar phase of triple-point fermions
arxiv-2107-00171.creator: Subrata Mandal and Igor F. Herbut
arxiv-2107-00171.description: Abstract We consider weak-coupling superconductivity in the inversion- and rotation-symmetric system of two pseudospin s = 1 s=1 low-energy fermions of opposite chirality. General contact interactions can lead to Cooper instabilities towards d-wave or towards a novel 2 × 3 2\times 3 p-wave matrix order parameter. We compute the Ginzburg-Landau free energy for the latter.

arxiv-2202-02485.title: Sharpness of C 0 C^{0} conjugacy for the non-autonomous differential equations with Lipschitzian perturbation This paper was jointly supported from the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant (No. 11671176, 11931016) and Grant Fondecyt 1170466.
arxiv-2202-02485.creator: Weijie Lu Manuel Pinto Y-H. Xia
arxiv-2202-02485.description: Abstract The classical C 0 C^{0} linearization theorem for the non-autonomous differential equations states the existence of a C 0 C^{0} topological conjugacy between the nonlinear system and its linear part. That is, there exists a homeomorphism (equivalent function) H H sending the solutions of the nonlinear system onto those of its linear part.

arxiv-2206-00414.creator: John D. Gibbon, Kolluru Venkata Kiran, Nadia Bihari Padhan, Rahul Pandit
arxiv-2206-00414.description: Abstract The incompressible Toner-Tu (ITT) partial differential equations (PDEs) are an important example of a set of active-fluid PDEs. While they share certain properties with the Navier-Stokes equations (NSEs), such as the same scaling invariance, there are also important differences.

arxiv-2305-07350.title: Detecting Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior in Likes on Social Media: Proof of Concept
arxiv-2305-07350.creator: Affiliations blinded for Review, Laura Jahn, Rasmus K. Rendsvig, Jacob Stærk-Østergaard
arxiv-2305-07350.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Affiliations blinded for Review, Laura Jahn, Rasmus K. Rendsvig, Jacob Stærk-Østergaard. Coordinated inauthentic behavior is used as a tool on social media to shape public opinion by elevating or suppressing topics using systematic engagements—e.g. through ‘likes’ or similar reactions. In an honest world, reactions may be informative to users when selecting on what to spend their attention: through the wisdom of crowds, summed reactions may help identifying relevant and high-quality content. This is nullified by coordinated inauthentic liking.

arxiv-2410-23191.title: Continuous Spatio-Temporal Memory Networks for 4D Cardiac Cine MRI Segmentation
arxiv-2410-23191.creator: Meng Ye, Bingyu Xin, Leon Axel, Dimitris Metaxas
arxiv-2410-23191.description: Abstract Current cardiac cine magnetic resonance image (cMR) studies focus on the end diastole (ED) and end systole (ES) phases, while ignoring the abundant temporal information in the whole image sequence. This is because whole sequence segmentation is currently a tedious process and inaccurate.

arxiv-2412-09694.title: Omni-ID: Holistic Identity Representation Designed for Generative Tasks
arxiv-2412-09694.creator: Guocheng Qian, Kuan-Chieh Wang, Or Patashnik, Negin Heravi, Sergey Tulyakov, Daniel Cohen-Or, Kfir Aberman
arxiv-2412-09694.description: Abstract We introduce Omni-ID, a novel facial representation designed specifically for generative tasks. Omni-ID encodes holistic information about an individual’s appearance across diverse expressions and poses within a fixed-size representation. It consolidates information from a varied number of unstructured input images into a structured representation, where each entry represents certain global or local identity features.

pmc-10670198.title: Colorectal Liver Metastasis: Can Cytokines Make the Difference?
pmc-10670198.creator: Costanza Ballarò, Valeria Quaranta, Gianluigi Giannelli, David A Geller, Serge Roche
pmc-10670198.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Simple SummaryColorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common malignancies worldwide, with a mortality rate of 86%. The main cause of death is the development of colorectal liver metastases (CRLMs). The communication between cancer cells and the environment is a prerequisite for generating a favorable tumor microenvironment, and it is mediated by soluble molecules such as cytokines, growth factors, and extracellular vesicles. Mounting evidence suggests that cytokines play a decisive role in CRC progression and metastasis.

pmc-11352857.description: The distinct clinical and radiological characteristics of right temporal variant FTD have only been recently recognized. Methods: Eight patients with right temporal variant FTD were prospectively recruited and underwent a standardised neuropsychological assessment, clinical MRI, and quantitative neuroimaging. Results: Our voxelwise grey analyses captured bilateral anterior and mesial temporal grey matter atrophy with a clear right-sided predominance.

pmc-12567005.title: Biocompatible Interpenetrating Network Hydrogels with Dually Cross-Linked Polyol
pmc-12567005.creator: Ulygbek B. Tuleuov, Alexander L. Kwiatkowski, Akerke T. Kazhmuratova, Lyazzat Zh. Zhaparova, Yermauyt Nassikhatuly, Miroslav Šlouf, Andrey V. Shibaev, Viktor I. Petrenko, Senentxu Lanceros-Méndez, Yerkeblan M. Tazhbayev
pmc-12567005.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Modern tissue regeneration strategies rely on soft biocompatible materials with adequate mechanical properties to support the growing tissues. Polymer hydrogels have been shown to be available for this purpose, as their mechanical properties can be controllably tuned. In this work, we introduce interpenetrating polymer networks (IPN) hydrogels with improved elasticity due to a dual cross-linking mechanism in one of the networks.

pmc-13373072.title: Non-canonical and induced neoantigens as emerging sources of cancer-specific immunotherapy targets
pmc-13373072.creator: Viacheslav V. Kudriavskii, Valeriia A. Koss, Victoria O. Shender, Georgij P. Arapidi
pmc-13373072.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment, yet its clinical benefit remains limited in many tumors, particularly those with low mutational burden. Because most current immunotherapeutic strategies rely on neoantigen recognition, expanding the repertoire of targetable tumor-specific antigens is essential. In this review, we discuss non-canonical and therapy-induced neoantigens – derived from alternative splicing, RNA editing, transposable elements, and aberrant translation – as emerging sources of immunotherapy targets, with emphasis on their potential to improve the efficacy of current treatment approaches.
